claim: Google announced on 22 Apr 2025 that Chrome will keep third-party cookies and will not ship a standalone choice prompt.
quote: we've made the decision to maintain our current approach to offering users third-party cookie choice in Chrome, and will not be rolling out a new standalone prompt for third-party cookies.

claim: Trade press corroboration of Google's April 2025 reversal on the third-party cookie choice prompt.
quote: Google isn't launching a user choice prompt for third-party cookies in Chrome.

claim: Per-browser state: Chrome does not block third-party cookies by default; Firefox partitions them via Total Cookie Protection under ETP (default on); Safari applies ITP protections by default.
quote: Google Chrome doesn't block third-party cookies by default, only in Incognito mode, or when users explicitly set it to block third-party cookies via chrome://settings.

claim: Safari has blocked all cross-site cookies by default since Safari 13.1 / iOS 13.4 (24 Mar 2020), and points authenticated embeds at the Storage Access API.
quote: Cookies for cross-site resources are now blocked by default across the board.

claim: A 'site' is scheme + registrable domain (eTLD+1); different subdomains of the same registrable domain are same-site.
quote: a combination of the scheme, the TLD, and the part of the domain just before it (We call it TLD+1) ... different subdomains don't matter

claim: Hosting app and IdP under the same registrable domain keeps the IdP first-party and lets iframe-based silent session restoration work; cross-site it does not, and the library falls back to a full-page redirect.
quote: the browser considers the IdP third-party to your app, it often refuses to attach those cookies in an embedded context (iframe)

claim: Keycloak's own JS adapter documents that Session Status iframe and silent check-sso are unsupported when third-party cookies are blocked, and that those features may ultimately be deprecated.
quote: the adapter cannot use a session cookie for Single Sign-Out detection and must rely purely on tokens ... As a result, the affected adapter features might ultimately be deprecated.

claim: keycloak.js silent check-sso and the check-session iframe break under third-party cookie blocking, causing phantom logouts; FedCM in Keycloak 26.x is not production-ready.
quote: FedCM support in Keycloak 26.x is emerging and actively tracked, but not a fully supported, production-ready feature.

claim: FedCM support in Keycloak is still an open discussion, not a shipped feature.
quote: Add support for FedCM (Federated Credential Management API)

claim: Duende documents that OIDC Session Management and OIDC Silent Login both break under third-party cookie blocking, and that the BFF replaces them with back-channel logout.
quote: OIDC Session Management allows a client SPA to monitor the session at the OP by reading a cookie from the OP in a hidden iframe.

claim: Chrome Enterprise admins can force third-party cookies to be allowed for specific third-party/top-level site pairs via the CookiesAllowedForUrls policy.
quote: set specific top-level sites to allow third-party cookies by adding each of them with a comma-separated third-party/top-level site pair to the CookiesAllowedForUrls policy.

claim: Chrome holds roughly 65% of global browser share, Safari roughly 18%, Edge above 5%, Firefox around 3% in 2026.
quote: Browser Market Share Worldwide

claim: RFC 9700 (BCP 240, Jan 2025) requires refresh tokens issued to public clients to be sender-constrained or rotated, with reuse detection revoking the token family and a maximum lifetime.
quote: Refresh tokens for public clients MUST be sender-constrained or use refresh token rotation

claim: RFC 9449 (DPoP, Sept 2023) requires refresh tokens issued to public clients presenting a DPoP proof to be bound to that public key, and notes non-extractable keys prevent exfiltration.
quote: When an authorization server supporting DPoP issues a refresh token to a public client that presents a valid DPoP proof at the token endpoint, the refresh token MUST be bound to the respective public key.

claim: Auth0's reference implementation of reuse detection revokes the entire descendant token family when a used refresh token is replayed.
quote: all refresh tokens descending from the original refresh token issued for the client

claim: Keycloak's refresh-token rotation revokes all token families for the client when the same app is open in multiple tabs; the issue was closed as 'not planned'.
quote: Refresh token rotation used with an app opened in multiple web browser tabs causes revocation of everything

claim: CVE-2026-9802: a Keycloak server restart resets startupTime and lets previously rotated refresh tokens be redeemed again when revokeRefreshToken=true; fixes targeted at 26.4.13 / 26.6.3 / 26.7.0.
quote: After a server restart, the startup time resets to the current moment, which causes the stale token validation to be bypassed for all previously rotated refresh tokens

claim: Keycloak refresh-token rotation is configured in Realm Settings > Tokens via 'Revoke Refresh Token' plus 'Refresh Token Max Reuse' = 0; defaults are 30 min SSO Session Idle, 10 h SSO Session Max, 5 min Access Token Lifespan.
quote: set Refresh Token Max Reuse to 0 (combined with Revoke Refresh Token for OIDC clients) to block replay attacks.

claim: OpenIddict enables rolling (rotating) refresh tokens by default with a 15-second reuse leeway to survive concurrent refreshes, configurable via SetRefreshTokenReuseLeeway() / DisableRollingRefreshTokens().
quote: The rolling refresh tokens mechanism now allows for a small leeway to avoid revoking entire token chains when concurrent requests are received (by default, it is set to 15 seconds but can be changed using OpenIddictServerBuilder.SetRefreshTokenReuseLeeway())

claim: DPoP became an officially supported (no longer preview) Keycloak feature in 26.4, including binding only refresh tokens for public clients and dpop_jkt in authorization requests.
quote: With the release of Keycloak 26.4, we're happy to share that OAuth 2.0 Demonstrating Proof-of-Possession (DPoP) is now officially supported.

claim: Keycloak documents how to enable DPoP-bound tokens per client ('Require DPoP bound tokens' switch).
quote: Securing applications with Demonstrating Proof-of-Possession (DPoP)

claim: As of June 2026, OpenIddict supports DPoP on the issuance side but its validation/resource-server stack extracts Bearer tokens only and validates proof-of-possession via mTLS only.
quote: OpenIddict fully supports DPoP on the server (issuance) side ... However, the validation / resource-server stack has no DPoP support at all.

claim: OpenIddict supports mTLS client authentication and certificate-bound (cnf.x5t#S256) access tokens in its server and validation stacks.
quote: Mutual TLS authentication

claim: InfoQ (30 Apr 2026): a non-extractable WebCrypto key still leaves a signing oracle reachable from XSS, Firefox cannot persist CryptoKey objects in IndexedDB, and the article concludes the BFF pattern is the safest browser option today.
quote: A non-extractable key is a key whose bytes you cannot export. It is not a key that cannot be used. ... The BFF pattern is the safest choice today for browser-based applications.

claim: oidc-client-ts implements RFC 9449 DPoP with an IndexedDbDPoPStore holding a non-extractable CryptoKeyPair, plus bind_authorization_code and UserManager.dpopProof().
quote: IndexedDb is used as storage because it is the only storage mechanism that is available that allows for storing CryptoKeyPair objects with non-extractable private keys securely

claim: oidc-spa ships DPoP with an 'auto' mode that installs fetch/XHR interceptors, officially supports Keycloak 26.4+, and notes Microsoft Entra ID does not support DPoP.
quote: Keycloak: Officially supported starting with version 26.4 ... Microsoft EntraID does not support DPoP yet

claim: The Storage Access API workaround for iframe silent renew requires an explicit user gesture (button click) in Firefox, and remains an unmerged proof-of-concept in oidc-client-ts.
quote: Make sure there is IFrame request End User to access Storage Access via Button Click

claim: Practitioners report iframe silent renewal failing in modern browsers with opaque iframe console errors, forcing full page reloads.
quote: Does Silent Renewal Using iFrames Work with Modern Browsers?

claim: react-oidc-context is the React binding for oidc-client-ts.
quote: React context provider for oidc-client-ts

claim: TanStack Query maintainer TkDodo advises handling token refresh in an HTTP-layer interceptor rather than in QueryCache/MutationCache onError.
quote: I would rather use an interceptor on the API layer for that.

claim: Concurrent queries each hitting 401 fire duplicate refresh calls; the async-mutex/async-lock question in TanStack Query remains unanswered.
quote: To update the refresh token for 401 status and for more than 2 requests. I couldn't connect with async-mutex or async-lock via interceptors axios.

claim: TanStack Query retries failed queries 3 times by default with exponential backoff capped at 30 s; retry: false disables it.
quote: will automatically retry the query if that query's request has not reached the max number of consecutive retries (defaults to 3)

claim: QueryCache global onError fires once per query rather than once per observer, and useQuery's onError callback was removed in v5.
quote: This will now only show an error toast once for each query, which exactly what we want.

claim: The failed-queue (single-flight) pattern is required or simultaneous 401s trigger multiple concurrent refresh calls and race conditions.
quote: The failed queue pattern is important — without it, multiple simultaneous 401s would trigger multiple refresh calls, causing race conditions.

claim: Naive axios interceptors with no shared state fired the refresh call 6-10 times at once on page reopen in a real codebase.
quote: the refresh token request was being made around 6-10 times at once when reopening the site

claim: A BFF holds tokens in a server-side session, refreshes the access token automatically when close to expiry, and needs a server-side session store for back-channel logout and to avoid the 4 KB cookie limit.
quote: the access token is retrieved from the session. If it is expired or close to expiring, BFF automatically refreshes it using the refresh token.

claim: keycloak-js, the official Keycloak JavaScript adapter, has minimal community traction compared with the generic OIDC clients.
quote: Keycloak JavaScript adapter

claim: oidc-spa is a React-oriented OIDC client that automates the third-party-cookie fallback and DPoP.
quote: Openid Connect client for Single Page Applications

claim: @auth0/auth0-react is the Auth0-specific React SDK, unusable against Keycloak/OpenIddict.
quote: Auth0 SDK for React Single Page Applications
